text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The government is drafting a bill to cut wage taxes, Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said on Friday during a meeting with a trade union confederation. He said the cabinet also planned to slash the value added tax.
- The stage of reforms in Romania does not qualify the country for the first wave of NATO expansion, President Emil Constantinescu told a conference in Bucharest.
- East Europe does not need a new Marshall Plan, but rather fast privatisation and solid foreign investment, Constantinescu told journalists during a visit to The Hague last week.
- Consumption of food and farm produce fell by 32 percent in the first quarter of 1997 from the same period last year.
- The government's new mining bill ends state monopoly of exploration and exploitation.

- The Labour Ministry is working out a bill to rise the monthly wages of the president, the prime minister and government members. Under the bill, Constantinescu would get a gross wage of 5.47 million lei, while Ciorbea would make a monthly 4.1 million lei.
- The deadline for privatisation bids for Petromidia refinery on the Black Sea coast has been pushed to June 30, State Ownership Fund's deputy director general Dan Mihut said.
- The court of accounts revealed tax evasion worth 376 billion lei from imports of cigarettes, coffee and alcohol over 1993-1995.
- Private investments in economy dropped by 41 percent in the first quarter due to the high interest rates on banking credits.
